(a) Any person who shall do or engage in any of the following in the unincorporated area of the county shall be guilty of disorderly conduct:
(1) Any person who shall act in a violent or tumultuous manner toward another, whereby any person is placed in danger of safety of his life, limb or health.
(2) Any person who shall act in a violent or tumultuous manner toward another, whereby public property of any other person is placed in danger of being destroyed or damaged.
(3) Any person who shall endanger lawful pursuits of another by acts of violence or threats of bodily harm.
(4) Any person who shall cause, provoke or engage in any fight, brawl or riotous conduct so as to endanger the life, limb, health or property of another or public property.
(5) Any person who shall assemble or congregate with another or others and cause, provoke or engage in any fight or brawl.
(6) Any person who shall collect in bodies or in crowds and engage in unlawful activities.
(7) Any person who shall assemble or congregate with another or others and engage or attempt to engage in gaming.
(8) Any person who shall frequent any public place and obtain money for another by an illegal and fraudulent scheme, trick, artifice or device, to attempt to do so.
(9) Any person who shall use "fighting words" directed towards any person who becomes outraged and thus creates turmoil.
(b) Any person or persons failing to comply with the mandatory provisions of this section or doing any act prohibited by this section shall be guilty of an offense of disorderly conduct and, upon conviction in the magistrate court of the county, shall be punished as provided in section 1-7 of this Code.
(Ord. of 2-5-91, §§ 1, 2)

(a) Gordon County, by and through the Gordon County Fire Department and/or the Gordon County Emergency Management Services Department, may seek recovery for all costs incurred in connection with the delivery of services, personnel, supplies and equipment to the scene of motor vehicle accidents and hazardous material emergencies, which costs shall be the actual costs incurred in accordance with a fee schedule properly approved by the Board of Commissioners of Gordon County. (c) All monies collected as a result of this section shall be placed into a fund as established by the Gordon County Board of Commissioners to be used exclusively for personnel, supplies and equipment for the Gordon County Fire Department.

Whenever a request is filed with the public nuisance officer (hereinafter referred to as "the officer") by a public authority, or by at least five (5) residents of the unincorporated area of the county, charging that any dwelling, building or structure in such area is unfit for human habitation or for commercial, industrial or business use or whenever it appears to the officer (on his own motion) that any dwelling, building or structure is unfit for human habitation or is unfit for its current commercial, industrial or business use or is vacant, dilapidated and being used in connection with the commission of drug crimes, the officer shall, if his preliminary investigation discloses a basis for such charges, issue and cause to be served upon the owner of and any parties in interest in such dwelling, building or structure a complaint stating the charges in that respect and containing a notice that a hearing will be held before the officer (or his designated agent) at a place within the county, fixed not less than ten (10) days nor more than thirty (30) days after the serving of the complaint; that the owner and any parties in interest shall be given the right to file an answer to the complaint and to appear in person or otherwise, and give testimony at the place and time fixed in the complaint; and that the rules of evidence prevailing in courts of law or equity shall not be controlling in hearings before the officer.

Automobile wrecking or automobile parts or automobile salvage yard, business or establishment includes any building, establishment, premises or other area where the business is carried on of stripping old or used automobiles or late model wrecks, or other motor vehicles which have been legally equipped for that purpose, and adding or employment of the accessories and parts thereof in equipping, repairing or rebuilding motor vehicles, or storing, selling or otherwise disposing of such accessories or parts; provided further, such yard, business or establishment is a commercial enterprise wherein late model automobiles which have been wrecked or abandoned and legally acquired by the operator of such yard, business or establishment, or his lawful agent, are stripped of their usable parts and sold as used parts either upon the wholesale or retail market; provided further, such yard, business or establishment is not a junk yard within the meaning of this article.
Fenced area means a solid partition or an opaque screening not less than six (6) feet in height through which the enclosed area cannot be seen.
Junk means any used items of commerce which principally comprises iron, steel, brass, copper, zinc or their alloys or any other base metals and which is commonly bought for the purpose of resale and refabrication, either or both (see O.C.G.A. § 43-22-1). The term "junk" also means worn out and discarded material that may be returned to some use, especially old rope, chain, iron, copper, parts of machinery, electrical and electronics equipment and bottles gathered or bought up by tradesmen called junk dealers, hence rubbish of any kind, odds and ends.
Junk business means the pursuit for profit of purchasing old iron, brass, bottles and things of that sort and selling them again in the condition in which the were purchased by the dealer.
Junk dealer means any person having a fixed place of business, or officer, agent and employee of any person who engages in the purchase of used items of commerce principally composed of iron, steel, brass, copper, zinc or their alloys or any other base metals and which is commonly bought for the purpose of resale and refabrication, either or both.
Salvage operation or salvage yard means a business, the principal activity of which is buying, selling, exchanging, storing, sorting, packing or dismantling of waste, used or secondhand materials or vehicles or parts thereof to consumers for personal use with only incidental residual transfer on a nonretail basis. An automobile wrecking establishment and a junk dealer are engaged in salvage operations.
Scrap means scrap iron and scrap steel or other base metals and secondhand materials which are only fit for remanufacturing or reprocessing without reference to whether it is new or old. Scrap metal and glass having no commercial value except for remelting purposes shall be considered scrap.
Scrap yard operator or scrap dealer means any person or his agent engaging, in a fixed location, in the purchase of scrap iron or steel and other base materials for the purpose of cutting or baling or otherwise preparing the same for sale to mills for remelting, with only incidental residual transfer on a retail basis.
(Ord. of 3-19-91, § III)
483:
The investigation and enforcement of the separate provisions of this article or any rule promulgated pursuant thereto shall be the responsibility of the county ordinance officer, who shall be authorized, empowered, and directed to enforce compliance with all provisions of this article in the unincorporated areas of the county, and on or in county-owned or operated facilities or property, in accordance with all applicable laws of the state. A fine of up to five hundred dollars ($500.00) shall be imposed for each violation of any part of this article for each day that an operator of an establishment authorized by this article is in violation of any part of this article.
(Ord. of 3-19-91, § IV; Mo. of 4-16-96)
484:
The jurisdiction for actions brought pursuant to this article shall be in the magistrate court of the county. Any appeal from errors in judgment by the enforcing officials shall be taken to the board of commissioners. All other appeals shall be in accordance with the Official Code of Georgia.
(Ord. of 3-19-91, § V)
485:
(a) If any term, part, provision, section, subdivision, paragraph, sentence, phrase or word of this article conflicts with any term, part, provision, section, subdivision, paragraph, sentence, phrase or word of any other county or state code, ordinance or statute, though legally valid and effective, that term, part, provision, section, subdivision, paragraph, sentence, phrase or word which sets the higher standards shall be the valid one. 487:

Any electrical or electronics equipment received by any operator of any operation or establishment authorized by this article shall be handled as prescribed in this section.
(Ord. of 3-19-91, § VIII)
488:

(Ord. of 3-19-91, § IX)
489:

490:
The premises of any operation or establishment authorized by this article shall be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition and shall be kept free of materials which tend to attract insects, rodents and vermin.
(Ord. of 3-19-91, § XI)
491:
Storage of vehicle bodies or assemblies or other junk, scrap metal or salvage materials shall be in accordance with this article; provided further, vehicles and materials being processed or intended for processing shall not be parked, stored or displayed outside of the fence surrounding the premises, on a public right-of-way, or on roofs of buildings.
(Ord. of 3-19-91, § XII)
493:
(a) Required generally. Investigating officials:
Building inspector
Fire chief
Health officer
Public nuisance officer
(Ord. of 3-19-91, § XIV)
494:
A permit for any operation or establishment authorized by this article shall terminate one year from the date of issuance and shall thereafter be void. A permit issued pursuant to this article may not be transferred from the permit recipient to another party. An application for renewal of a permit shall be granted upon written application, made and processed in the same manner as required in the instance of the original application for such permit, and the fee shall be twenty-five dollars ($25.00) for each permit location. Any person holding a permit for any operation or establishment as authorized by this article who shall discontinue business for a period exceeding ninety (90) days shall thereby be deemed to have relinquished all his rights and interest in or under the permit, and the permit shall automatically become null and void. It shall not be reinstated or reissued except in the same manner as required in the instance of the issuance of the original permit; provided further, that no fee or prorated part thereof shall be refunded, but the board of commissioners may reduce the permit fee to twelve dollars and fifty cents ($12.50) upon any application for a permit which has six (6) months or less to run before the beginning of the next permit year, January first to December thirty-first annually.
(Ord. of 3-19-91, § XV)
495:
(a) State license. In addition to the requirements of this article, the applicant for any operation or establishment authorized by this article shall provide, as a part of the process of applying for or renewing a permit, a license issued by the state board of registration for used motor vehicle dismantlers, rebuilders and salvage dealers (see O.C.G.A. § 43-48-1 et seq.).

Any permit granted shall be on condition that the applicant shall, within thirty (30) days after the site shall have ceased to be used as a scrap, salvage, junk, equipment and material storage or parts yard, or any other operation or establishment as authorized by this article, restore such site to a safe, clean and presentable condition, to the satisfaction of the building inspector and health officer. This bond shall be in the amount of one thousand dollars ($1,000.00). In order to guarantee the faithful performance of such bond, the applicant shall deposit with the county either cash, a certified check, a letter of credit in the amount of such bond or other good and valuable security as determined by the board of commissioners.

(Ord. of 3-19-91, § XVI)
496:
No business license fee is authorized by this article, and the fee charged for a permit to maintain yards, establishments and operations as described in this article is not to be constructed as a license to engage in any such commercial business.
(Ord. of 3-19-91, § XVII)
497:
Any operation or establishment authorized by this article which is or may become nonconforming with respect to location or use, or both location and use, or which may become nonconforming through a subsequent rezoning or change of regulations, may continue to operate only by permission of the board of commissioners.
(Ord. of 3-19-91, § XVIII)
500:
(1) Upon the declaration of a state of emergency by the governor, or upon the determination by the county governing authority or its designee of the existence of an emergency or disaster, the county governing authority, its designee or the emergency interim successor may adopt a resolution instituting a curfew when it is determined necessary to protect and safeguard the people and property of Gordon County.
(2) All of the territory of the unincorporated county shall be subject to the terms of the curfew, unless otherwise specified in the resolution.
(3) The resolution instituting the curfew shall include the dates and hours that the curfew shall be in effect.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(1), § 1)
501:
(1) Curfew. A "curfew" is a regulation requiring the withdrawal from any person not otherwise exempt from this article from appearing in certain public areas during specified hours.
(2) Exempt individuals. Unless otherwise specified in the resolution implementing the curfew, "exempt individuals" include those individuals engaged in the provision of designated essential services such as fire, law enforcement, emergency medical services and hospital services, military services, [and/or] utility emergency repairs. The resolution may, in the discretion of the governing authority, also exempt regular employees of local industries traveling to and from their jobs with appropriate identification, news media employees, building and repair contractors, properly registered according to article V, performing activities related to construction, repair, renovation or improvement of buildings and other structures damaged during the disaster or emergency.
(3) State of emergency. As defined by O.C.G.A. § 38-3-3(5), a condition declared by the governor when, in his judgment, the threat or actual occurrence of a disaster, emergency, or energy emergency is of sufficient severity and magnitude as to warrant extraordinary efforts in preventing or alleviating the damage, loss, hardship, or suffering threatened or caused thereby.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(1), § 2)
502:
It shall be prohibited for any person, other than exempt individuals, to appear in public in the territory subject to the curfew, including but not limited to, streets, highways, alleys, sidewalks, vacant lots, parks, public buildings or any other public places in all or a delineated part of unincorporated Gordon County during the stated hours of the curfew.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(1), § 3)
503:
Any individual violating this ordinance, upon conviction, shall be punishable by a fine not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) per violation or imprisonment not to exceed sixty (60) days, or both.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(1), § 4)
506:
(1) Meetings. Upon proclamation by the appropriate state official of an emergency or disaster of manmade or natural causes or enemy attack impending on or affecting Georgia or the United States, the affairs and business of Gordon County may be conducted at places other than the regular or usual place thereof, within or outside of Gordon County, when it is not prudent, expedient or possible to conduct business at the regular location. When such meetings occur outside of Gordon County, all actions taken by the local governing body shall be as valid and binding as if performed within Gordon County. Such meetings may be called by the presiding officer or any two (2) members of the governing body without regard to or compliance with time-consuming procedures and formalities otherwise required by law.
(2) Purchasing and public works contracts. Upon the declaration of a state of emergency by the governor, or upon the determination by the county governing authority or its designee of the existence of an emergency or disaster, the county governing authority, its designee or the emergency interim successor may contract for public works without letting such contract out to the lowest, responsible bidder and without advertising and posting notification of such contract for four (4) weeks; provided, however, that any public works contract entered into pursuant to this subsection shall be entered on the minutes of the county as soon as practical and the nature of the emergency described therein.
(3) Code enforcement. Upon the declaration of a state of emergency by the governor, or upon the determination by the county governing authority or its designee of the existence of an emergency or disaster, the county governing authority, its designee or the emergency interim successor may temporarily suspend the enforcement of the Code of Ordinances of Gordon County, or any portion thereof, where:
(a) The emergency or disaster is of such nature that immediate action outside the Code is required;
(b) Such suspension is consistent with the protection of the public health, safety and welfare; and
(c) Such suspension is not inconsistent with any federal or state statutes or regulations.
(4) Fees. Upon the declaration of a state of emergency by the governor, or upon the determination by the county governing authority or its designee of the existence of an emergency or disaster, the county governing authority, its designee or the emergency interim successor may temporarily reduce or suspend any permit fees, application fees or other rate structures as necessary to encourage the rebuilding of the area impacted by the disaster or emergency.
(5) Temporary dwellings. Upon the declaration of a state of emergency by the governor, or upon the determination by the county governing authority or its designee of the existence of an emergency or disaster, the county governing authority, its designee or the emergency interim successor may issue [authorize] temporary mobile home, trailer, recreational vehicle or other temporary dwelling structures or parks in any zoning district while the primary dwelling is being repaired provided that such temporary dwellings or parks are designed by an engineer and the plans are approved by the Gordon County Health Department and Gordon [County] Building and Inspections Department. The temporary permit shall not exceed six (6) [months] in duration. In the case of continuing hardship and in the discretion of the governing authority or its designee, the permit may be extended for a period for an additional six (6) months. Upon expiration of the temporary permit or an extension, the temporary dwelling shall be removed.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(2), § 1)
507:
(1) Fees. Any fee or rate charged by the county for building permits, land disturbance permits, zoning applications, special land use permits, temporary land use permits, and other fees relating to the reconstruction, repair and cleanup of areas impacted by the disaster or emergency. "Fees" shall not include those fees collected by the county on behalf of the federal or state government or those fees charged by the county pursuant to a federal or state statute or regulation.
(2) State of emergency. As defined by O.C.G.A. § 38-3-3(5), a condition declared by the governor when, in his judgment, the threat or actual occurrence of a disaster, emergency, or energy emergency is of sufficient severity and magnitude as to warrant extraordinary efforts in preventing or alleviating the damage, loss, hardship, or suffering threatened or caused thereby.
(3) Subsequent recovery period. The period of time that the disaster or emergency continues to cause disruptions in the area impacted by the disaster or emergency. The "subsequent recovery period" shall not exceed six (6) months after the state of emergency declaration by the governor is terminated unless extended by official action of the governing authority of [Gordon] County.
(4) Temporary dwelling. Any mobile or easily movable home, trailer, recreational vehicle or structure not otherwise permitted by the zoning regulations in a particular zoning district.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(2), § 2)
510:
In order to preserve, protect, or sustain the life, health, or safety of persons or their property, it shall be unlawful during the duration of a state of emergency or subsequent recovery period in which Gordon County has been designated as a disaster area, for any person, firm, or corporation located or doing business in Gordon County to overcharge for any goods, materials, services or housing sold within the county.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(3), § 1)
511:
(1) Overcharging. The term "overcharging" is defined as charging prices for goods, materials, services, or housing which are substantially in excess of the customary charges or in applicable cases substantially in excess of the supplier's or provider's costs for such goods, materials, services or housing. The existence of overcharging shall be presumed from a substantial increase in the price at which the goods, materials, services, or housing was offered in the usual course of business immediately prior to the onset of the emergency, but shall not include increases in costs to the supplier directly attributable to higher costs of materials, supplies, and labor costs resulting from the emergency.
(2) State of emergency. The term "state of emergency" is defined, pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 38-3-3(5), as a condition declared by the governor when, in his judgment, the threat or actual occurrence of a disaster or emergency is of sufficient severity and magnitude as to warrant extraordinary efforts in preventing or alleviating the damage, loss, hardship, or suffering threatened or caused thereby.
(3) Subsequent recovery period. The term "subsequent recovery period" is defined as that period during which the disaster continues to cause disruptions in the disaster area, but shall not exceed six (6) months after the emergency declaration has been terminated by the governor unless extended by official action of the governing authority of Gordon County.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(3), § 2)
512:
Violation of the provisions of this article upon conviction shall be punishable by a fine not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) per violation or imprisonment not to exceed sixty (60) days, or both such fine and imprisonment. Each sale shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(3), § 3)
515:
No person, firm, partnership, corporation or other entity shall engage in, undertake or carry on any business in whole or in part within the unincorporated areas of Gordon County consisting of or relating to building, constructing, repairing, renovating or making improvements to real property including dwellings, homes, buildings, structures, or fixtures attached thereto without having registered the name of the business with the governing authority of the county and having paid fees as provided by this article.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(4), § 1)
516:
(1) Building contractor. As used in this article, the word or term "building contractor" shall mean any person, firm, partnership, corporation or other entity engaging in, undertaking or carrying on any business consisting of or relating to building construction, repair, renovation or making improvements to real property including dwellings, homes, buildings, structures, or fixtures attached thereto.

(4) Subsequent recovery period. The term "subsequent recovery period" is defined as that period during which the disaster continues to cause disruptions in the disaster area, but shall not exceed three (3) months after the emergency declaration has been terminated by the governor.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(4), § 2)
517:
All building contractors doing business or proposing to do business in the unincorporated areas of Gordon County during a state of emergency or the subsequent recovery period shall register and file applications with the clerk of the governing authority of the county or such other person designated by the governing authority at the county courthouse or such other place or places designated by the county. The building contractor shall, under oath, provide the county governing authority with a statement describing the general nature of the business to be conducted and give true and correct information as may be called for on the registration form, application or certificate provided by the county.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(4), § 3)
518:
Building contractor registration fees are hereby fixed under the terms and conditions of this article at fifty dollars ($50.00) per annum. Registration fees shall be paid in full at the time of issuance of the registration certification.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(4), § 4)
519:
Any building contractor required by this article to pay a registration fee who engages in business without first registering and receiving a registration certification from the county as required shall be in violation of this article. Violation of this article, upon conviction, shall be punishable by a fine not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) per violation and/or imprisonment not to exceed sixty (60) days. Each day a building contractor does business in the unincorporated areas of the county without complying with this article shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(4), § 5)
520:
Each certification issued under this article is granted to, and shall be accepted by, the building contractor under the condition that the same is not transferable and after issuance no such certification shall be transferred by the county or the building contractor to another individual or entity.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(4), § 6)
521:
Each certification issued hereunder shall be posted conspicuously by the building contractor in the place of business of the building contractor or shall be carried on his person or vehicle used in such business. Such certification shall be exhibited to any authorized enforcement officer when so requested.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(4), § 7)
522:
Each certification granted under this article is a mere permit to engage in the business only so long as said business is conducted in a lawful manner. The county governing authority hereby reserves the right to revoke or suspend any certification granted hereunder, if the building contractor, or the building contractor's agent or employee acting within the scope of his employment, violates this article or any other county, state or federal law. If after issuance of a certification, the county desires to revoke such certification, written notice thereof shall be given to the building contractor, which notice shall specify the violation with which the building contractor is charged and a date, time and place at which a hearing shall be held with regard to the violation. The building contractor shall have an opportunity to be heard at such hearing, shall have the right to be represented by counsel, and shall have the right to introduce and submit evidence in opposition to such revocation.
(Ord. of 10-9-01(4), § 8)

525:
The Gordon County Personnel Policies create a system of employment which recognizes that the county employees covered by the system should be selected and promoted according to their skills, knowledge and abilities, and that employees who perform satisfactorily should be retained in their positions as long as the positions exist and regardless of factors not associated with their performance and conduct compatible with the trust inherent in public service, the administrative necessity for the position held, availability of funds and organizational needs of the government unit.
(Ord. of 12-19-95, Ch. 1, § A)
526:
These policies have been established by the Gordon County Board of Commissioners, hereinafter referred to as the "board." The board and participating elected officials have included specified employees under their administration in the system. This action was taken to provide a fair, equitable, and productive work environment. The system and these policies have been enabled by the signatures of the participating elected officials and by an ordinance adopted by the board of commissioners.
(Ord. of 12-19-95, Ch. 1, § B)
527:
These policies have been adopted to provide for the recruitment and development of the best available employee for each position in the service of the county. They provide for the establishment of orderly procedures for administering the following principles:
(1) Recruiting, selecting and advancing employees on the basis of their relative ability, knowledge and skills, including open competition of qualified applicants for initial appointment.
(2) Establishing pay rates consistent with the principle of providing comparable pay for comparable work.
(3) Training employees, as needed, to assure high-quality performance.
(4) Retraining employees on the basis of the adequacy of their performance, correcting inadequate performance, and separating employees from the work force whose inadequate performance cannot be corrected.
(5) Assuring equal employment opportunity through the fair treatment of applicants and employees in all aspects of personnel administration without regard to political affiliation, race, color, creed, national origin or ancestry, disability, sex, or religion and with proper regard for their privacy and constitutional rights as citizens.
(6) Assuring that employees are protected against coercion for partisan political purposes and are prohibited from using their official authority for the purpose of interfering with or affecting the results of an election or a nomination for office.
(7) Establishing uniform benefits and personnel procedures where applicable.
(8) Complying with applicable federal and state laws.
(Ord. of 12-19-95, Ch. 1, § C)

528:
These policies apply to the career service positions in all departments under the administration of the board and of the participating elected officials, including those employees whose positions are subsidized from federal, state or other sources. The following are the exceptions:
(1) Federal equal employment law recognizes that neither elected officials nor members of their personal staffs should be covered by legislation creating full-time positions, and O.C.G.A. § 36-1-21 exempts elected officials or persons appointed to positions for specified terms from civil service coverage. 531:
For the purpose of explaining and clarifying the personnel policies of the county, the following words and phrases shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them by this section of word definitions.
Anniversary date is the date one (1) year from the initial employment date. For leave purposes, the anniversary date shall be that date each subsequent year from the initial date of employment.
Appeal means the right to appear before the county administrator, or his designee, or the appropriate authority so designated by this chapter to be heard on matters of discrimination, unfair practices, or other rights of applicants or employees under these policies and for review of decisions by the county.
Board of commissioners or board means the legislative body of the county.
Career service includes all jobs subject to the terms of the personnel policies, except for those specifically exempted.
Class means a group of positions sufficiently similar as to the duties performed, degree of supervision exercised or required, minimum requirements of training, experience, and such other characteristics, that the same title, the same tests of fitness, the same schedule of compensation may be applied to each position in the group; and which has been recognized as such in the classification plan established and approved by the county.
Continuous service is employment which is uninterrupted except for authorized leaves of absence, suspension, or separation due to a reduction in the work force.
Demotion means the reduction of a regular or working test employee to a position of a lower class. For this purpose, a lower class means a class having a minimum salary lower than the maximum salary for the position in which the individual is employed.
Department head means any county employee designated as the head or principal administrative officer of any department established in the internal organization of the county as an administrative medium of the county administrator and subordinate to the county administrator. For the purposes of this chapter, the term "department head" may also refer to an elected official or a judicial official.
Employee means an incumbent of a position as hereinafter defined.
Exempt employee means an employee who is exempt from the provisions of the wage and hour laws of the Fair Labor Standards Act. All department heads are considered to be exempt employees.
Full-time position means any employee in a regular position who is scheduled to work at least thirty (30) hours per week.
Merit increase means a pay adjustment earned due to length of service and satisfactory performance as determined by existing policies and available funding.
Nonexempt employee means an employee who is covered by the provisions of the wage and hour laws of the Fair Labor Standards Act.
Open competitive vacancy means a position wherein announcement of a vacancy and acceptance of applications is solicited from every segment of the community.
Part time means any employee working less than thirty (30) hours per week on a continuing basis.
Performance evaluation means a method of evaluating each employee on a periodic basis as to his performance on the job.
Position means a job, whether part-time or full-time, temporary or regular, occupied or vacant, composed of specific duties and responsibilities requiring the services of one (1) person.
Promotion means the filling of a vacancy by the advancement of a regular employee from a position of a lower class. For this purpose, a lower class means any class of positions having a maximum salary lower than the maximum salary of the vacant position.
Promotional competitive vacancy means a position wherein announcement of a vacancy and acceptance of applications is confined to employees of the county.
Public notice, unless otherwise expressly stated, means a written notice on a bulletin board accessible to the public during business hours, and other publicity as may be deemed necessary by the county administrator or his designee.
Regular employee is an employee who has completed his working test period in a satisfactory manner and has obtained status in the career service.
Resignation means an action separating an employee at his own written or verbal request and is accepted without prejudice, provided that the resignation is not offered to avoid removal for cause. If a resignation is offered to avoid removal for cause, it will not be accepted as a resignation unless it is determined to be clearly in the best interest of the county. A resignation is effective immediately upon acceptance and no further administrative action is required to validate that resignation.
Salary advancement means an increase in salary, based on quality and length of service within the salary range prescribed for a particular class of positions.
Salary range adjustment means the allocation of a classification to a higher or lower salary range, due to legislative or administrative action.
Status is acquired by the satisfactory completion of a working test period by an employee in the classified service.
Suspension means the temporary removal of an employee from the county for either disciplinary purposes or pending investigation of charges against the employee. A suspension may be with or without pay.
Temporary employees means those engaged for special activities of the county for a specific period with the definite understanding that their employment is to terminate at the end of the period. Temporary employees will be considered either full-time or part-time, depending upon the number of hours worked per week. No temporary employee will be eligible to accrue privileges or benefits under the provisions of the fringe benefits, insurance and retirement plans.
Transfer means an action to change an employee from a position in one (1) department to a position in another department within the same classification or a change from one (1) class to another class in the same pay grade. Where an increase or decrease of pay grade is involved, the action will be designated as a "promotion" or a "demotion."
Vacancy is a position duly created and still existent but not occupied by an employee.
Working test period describes the status of a newly appointed or promoted employee who is required to serve a six-month working test period to demonstrate satisfactory job performance and who may be released from employment or returned to pre-promotion status without recourse.
(Ord. of 12-19-95, Ch. 1, § G)

536:
(a) Announcement of vacant positions. Vacancies shall be publicized by posting announcements at the county courthouse or in other places, and by such other means as the county administrator and the human resources director deem advisable for positions for which the county administrator is the hiring authority. Elected officials may establish their own policies for recruitment and selection of vacant positions. Receipt of applications may be limited to present employees or may be opened to the public. The announcements shall:
(1) Specify the title and salary range of the vacant positions, qualification requirements, manner of making application, and other pertinent information.
(2) Specify the form of the examination if required for the positions.
(b) Application forms. Application shall be made on forms provided by the human resources director. Such forms shall require information covering training, experience, and other pertinent information. All applications shall be signed by the applicant.
(c) Employment requirements. All positions shall be open to persons who meet the requirements as listed on the public announcement of the examination. Such requirements may include, but shall not be limited to, the following factors:
(1) Experience.
(2) Education.
(3) Training.
(d) Receipt and duration of applications. Applications will be accepted only when there is an advertised opening for a position. The applications will be placed on file from all persons desiring employment with the county, and who apply during regular business hours. In order to be considered for employment, all applicants for employment must complete an employment application. All persons shall be informed at the time of application that applications will be placed in an active file for a period of forty-five (45) days. Should another position become available during the forty-five-day period for which a rejected applicant wishes to be considered, the rejected applicant should contact the human resources director and request consideration.
(e) Rejection of applications. The human resources director may reject an application which indicates that the applicant is deficient in any or all of the requirements as specified in the public announcement of the vacancy. An application may also be rejected for the practice, or attempted practice, of fraud or deception in the completion of his application or if his past record of employment is determined by the human resources director to be unsatisfactory. Notice of rejection, stating the reason therefor, shall be mailed to the rejected applicant by the human resources director.
(f) Open competitive appointments. Positions to be filled by recruitment, from outside the career service, shall be filled through a competitive process open to the public. Such process may include, but not be limited to, ratings of training and experience, written, oral, physical, or performance tests, or any combination of these as determined by the human resources director. The process may take into consideration such factors as education, experience, knowledge, skill, physical fitness, or any other bona fide occupational qualifications which are job-related and which, in the judgment of the human resources director, enter into the determination of the relative suitability of applicants. The human resources director may require the applicant to submit proof of his education, military service, or any other such documentation as he/she deems necessary. All qualifications and tests shall be job-related and shall be administered in a nondiscriminatory manner.
(g) Promotional appointments. Promotional appointments shall be open to all employees, who meet the training and experience requirements included in the class specification, or who have an equivalent combination of experience and training which provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities.

537:
(a) Types of appointments. When a person is initially employed by the county, they shall be given one (1) of the following types of original appointments:
(1) Working test. An appointment to a position in the career service.
(2) Provisional. An appointment made only in the absence of a qualified applicant.
a. When there is a need to fill a vacancy, and a qualified applicant is not available, a provisional appointment may be made.
b. Provisional appointments shall not exceed six (6) months. However, extensions may be approved by the county administrator, elected official, or judicial official, where applicable.
c. An employee shall not attain regular status while serving on a provisional appointment.
(3) Temporary. Temporary appointments may be made to fill positions when the work of the county requires the services of one (1) or more employees on a seasonal or intermittent basis, or in cases of emergency. Temporary appointments shall not exceed one (1) year's consecutive duration.
(b) Regular appointment. A career employee, given an original working test appointment, shall be given a regular appointment upon satisfactory completion of the working test period and shall acquire regular status. A working test promotional appointment does not affect an employee's earned regular status and rights acquired in another position.
(c) Hiring authority. The county administrator shall serve as the hiring authority for all positions, except for those positions in the department of the elected officials and the judicial officials. The elected officials and the judicial officials shall serve as the hiring authority in their respective departments. Prior to extending an offer of employment to any person as a department head, the county administrator shall make a recommendation to and receive approval from the board of commissioners for that offer of employment as a department head. The board of commissioners, based upon the recommendation of the county administrator, shall approve said offer of employment as a department head by a majority vote, with at least three (3) commission members affirming the recommendation of the county administrator. In addition, prior to advertising any newly created position for county employment, the county administrator shall likewise obtain approval by a majority vote of the board of commissioners, with at least three (3) commission members voting in the affirmative, for the advertisement of the newly created position.

538:
(a) Objective. The working test period shall be regarded as an integral part of the selection process and shall be utilized for closely observing the employee's work, for securing the most effective adjustment of a new employee to his position, and for rejecting any employee whose performance is not satisfactory.
(b) Duration. The working test period shall be six (6) months in duration.
(c) Promotional appointments. The working test period shall be used in connection with promotional appointments in the same manner as it is used for original entrance appointments. If a person is removed during his working test period following a promotion, he may be considered for return to his former position, or a similar position, if one is available.
(d) Interruption of working test. If an employee is laid off during a working test period, and his services have been satisfactory and he is subsequently reemployed in the same department, he shall be given credit for the portion of the working test period completed before he was laid off.

A report in writing shall be sent to the human resources director within three (3) days after the effective date of the dismissal.
(2) An employee found to have been appointed through fraud shall be removed within ten (10) calendar days of notification of the department head to this effect.
(3) A department head may demote an employee to a lower class position during the working test period. A written report of such demotion and the reasons therefor must be filed with the human resources director within three (3) days after the effective date of the demotion.
(4) Working test period reports. At least twenty (20) working days prior to the expiration of the employee's working test period, the department head shall notify the human resources director, in writing, whether the employee has satisfactorily completed, or is expected to satisfactorily complete, his working test period.
(5) An employee may be released during the working test period without recourse and as such has no right to avail himself or herself to a grievance procedure.

(a) Objective. The county administrator may prepare, or cause to be prepared, a job-related system for evaluating the work performance of all employees in the career service. The purpose of the employee performance evaluation is primarily to inform employees of work performance and to provide guidance for work performance improvement. The performance evaluation may also be used in determining order of layoff, as a basis for training, promotion, demotion, transfer, or dismissal, and for such other purposes as set forth in these regulations or as determined appropriate by the county administrator so long as such is consistent with the provisions of these regulations.

An employee in a supervisory position, who is leaving the position, may be required to submit performance evaluation forms on all the employees under their supervision who have not been recently evaluated.

(2) The employee's supervisor, department head and human resources director;
(3) The county administrator or their designated representative; and
(4) Attorneys representing the county.
(f) Changes in evaluation. If for any reason a department head requests an alteration of the performance evaluation form, after it has been officially submitted to the human resources director, such request should be in writing and shall set forth fully the reasons for the request.
